data.title: iA Financial Group Chief Legal Officer Isabelle Durand Named In-House Legal Leader of the Year
data.description:
iA Financial Group is proud to congratulate Chief Legal Officer Isabelle Durand on being named In-House Legal Leader of the Year at a celebration held on October 8 in Toronto.

The award is part of the annual Canadian In-House Counsel Celebration and is co-presented by the Canadian Bar Association (CBA) In-House Lawyers and Legal 500. It honours legal leadership, strategic insight and legal expertise that advance ethical standards, innovation, and organizational and community goals.

For iA, this recognition speaks to something bigger: a legal function that helps the organization look ahead, navigate complexity and turn ambition into action.

“I am honoured to receive this recognition, which also reflects the expertise, commitment and collaborative spirit of our legal team,” said Isabelle Durand, Senior Vice-President and Chief Legal Officer at iA Financial Group. “Every day, our team works alongside our business partners to enable growth, strengthen sound decision-making and help iA manage legal risk with discipline. I am proud of what we continue to accomplish together.”

iA Financial Group’s legal team operates across Canada and the United States, with expertise spanning across all business lines as well as corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions, investments, litigation, commercial agreements, employment, regulatory matters and government relations. Recently, the team supported one of Canada’s largest acquisitions in wealth distribution, RF Capital Group Inc. (Richardson Wealth).

“Isabelle is a highly respected and trusted leader whose judgment, business acumen and collaborative approach have strengthened iA Financial Group,” said Stephanie Butt Thibodeau, Executive Vice-President, Talent and Corporate Affairs, iA Financial Group. “Under her leadership, our legal team has become an even stronger strategic partner to the business, supporting our growth while reinforcing sound governance and disciplined risk management. This national recognition is richly deserved. “

For more information about Isabelle Durand’s In-House Legal Leader of the Year recognition, visit Winners 2026—Events.

The In-House Legal Leader of the Year recognition reinforces iA’s ambition to build teams where talented professionals can take on meaningful challenges, broaden their impact and help shape what comes next.

About iA Financial Group

iA Financial Group is one of the largest insurance and wealth management groups in Canada, with operations in the United States. Founded in 1892, it is an important Canadian public company and is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol IAG (common shares).

To learn more about iA Financial Group, you can sign up for our newsletter on our website at ia.ca

iA Financial Group is a business name and trademark of iA Financial Corporation Inc.

data.title: Asian gasoline margin slides as Chinese barrels return
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins nearly halved on Friday from a record high hit at the beginning of the month, as Chinese refiners resumed fuel exports, easing immediate supply concerns, traders and analysts said.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline plummeted to about $24 per barrel over Brent crude from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1. However, the margin remains well above $13 a barrel recorded in October last year.

"Supply situation has improved at the prompt at least, as Chinese exports have returned," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects said.

"Also, refining runs in Asia, excluding China, are likely to increase in the fourth quarter, contributing to supplies", she added.

Gasoline cracks typically weaken during the winter months in the northern hemisphere due to lower demand, but a tight supply outlook due to a war in the Middle East, a Russian export ban and a few unplanned outages at regional refineries at a time when inventories were lower at key trading hubs drove margins to a record.

Restocking at key inventories like Singapore also helped ease supply concerns, even though Middle East shipments remained constrained, analysts said.

"Singapore light distillate inventories rose for a second consecutive week to a one-month high, pointing to improving product availability in Asia," LSEG Research said in a note.

Light distillate inventories, including naphtha and gasoline, rose to a one-month high of 13.806 million barrels in the week to October 14, Enterprise Singapore data showed on Thursday.

Gasoline imports into the major trading and blending hub rose about 11% to 320,000 tons or the equivalent of 2.7 million barrels during the period, while exports were down about 23% on the week at roughly 486,000 tons.

Gasoline inflows were led by China at nearly 177,000 tons, followed by Brunei at about 64,000 tons. Outbound volumes were led by Indonesia at about 221,000 tons, followed by Malaysia at around 105,000 tons.

The price for benchmark-grade fuel also eased to $129.20 per barrel on Friday from a near seven-month high of $150.69 per barrel touched on October 1; however, they were also seasonally at a higher level. (GL92-SIN)

data.title: U.S. Industrial Production Faces Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description:
1109 ET - A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." They add that manufacturing production rose "a more modest" 0.3%. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," Clark and Hollenhorst say. They add that higher interest rates and fading fiscal support represent headwinds to non-AI manufacturing into 2027. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1033 ET - Unlike in recent years, the British economy has sustained its early-year momentum into the second half of 2026, Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin says in a note. "This likely reflects a combination of genuine strength due to structural change because of IT-related investment, but also noisy data," he says. Rapid increases in AI usage mean recent IT strength will likely endure, though strong pickup in professional services output in the last six months is harder to explain. Any resilience will come under pressure over the next few quarters, particularly given most of the impact of the Middle East war is still to come. Financial conditions have worsened, and fiscal policy is being tightened, he adds. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

1026 ET - If Albertans and Quebecois did vote to leave Canada, what would that mean for the rest of the country? Capital Economics' Bradley Saunders argues the blow to GDP from losing Quebec industry and Alberta oil and gas could be mediated somewhat by continued free trade, companies relocating from seceding provinces to the rest of Canada and a weaker Canadian dollar boosting export competitiveness in other sectors. As such, the economist expects the rest of Canada to outperform the two provinces, whose newfound independence would likely require fiscal tightening. Of course secession would be a lengthy and complicated process without precedent and as such there remains a lot of uncertainty, Saunders says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1026 ET - Canada's housing market remains soft, with a combination of higher fixed mortgage rates and potential Bank of Canada tightening likely keeping buyers on the defensive, Bank of Montreal's Robert Kavcic says. The economist continues to argue that market pricing of a percentage point in interest rates increases in 2027 is too aggressive, but says the balance of risk is tilting to the upside for variable rates into the coming spring market for housing. "This poses an issue for the market given that variable rates are currently the lowest available by a relatively wide margin, and most buyers have pivoted to that space," he says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1024 ET - Elevated oil prices boosted Canada's purchasing power but the gains are uneven across the country, Royal Bank of Canada says. Real gross domestic income expanded 3.1% on-year in 2Q, nearly triple the pace of real GDP growth after a 46% surge in oil added about C$12 billion a quarter to export revenue. Royal Bank says oil producers and resource-rich provinces are capturing a disproportionate share of the initial windfall, while most households face higher costs without offsetting income gains. This complicates monetary policy, since the Bank of Canada controls only one interest rate for the entire country, Royal Bank adds. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1018 ET - The rise in mortgage rates has sent Canada's housing market into reverse, with sales and prices both falling in September, says Capital Economics' Stephen Brown. With the risk mortgage rate rise further prices could fall a bit more in the coming months, though Brown doesn't anticipate the Bank of Canada will lift its policy rate as aggressively as markets are pricing in. Lenders have been forced to pass on higher funding costs to fixed mortgage rates. Yet while home prices may fall near term, Brown says he is more upbeat about the outlook from mid-2027 as mortgage rates drop back next year. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1011 ET - The widening of spreads between French and German government bond yields has had as much, or possibly more, negative impact on the euro as widening Treasury-German spreads, Standard Chartered's Steve Englander says in a note. "Rising French credit default swaps (CDS) also have a significant impact on euro; although the relationship is not as tight as with the French-German spread, the CDS correlation still supports the view of concerns about France's government finances." The euro faces renewed depreciation if spreads widen further, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1256 after hitting a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0929 ET - The impact of the October 28 U.K. budget on sterling depends on the implications for economic growth and debt sustainability, Ebury's Matthew Ryan says in a note. A positive case for sterling would be restoring the fiscal headroom to around 15-20 billion pounds and modest spending increases with small, targeted take hikes and early revenue. "Less long-dated issuance would likely ease pressure on 30-year U.K. government bonds and provide the pound with modest upside." This would provide room for the Bank of England to raise interest rates in November, he says. A negative scenario would be a fiscal headroom of less than 15 billion pounds with bigger spending increases and back-loaded tax hikes with uncertain revenue, he says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0911 ET - The euro might struggle to sustain current gains against the dollar as French fiscal risks persist, Monex Europe analysts say in a note. The 10-year French-German government bond yield spread is off its early-October highs but there are ongoing tensions over the government's proposals to reduce the budget deficit. With the European Central Bank likely to keep rates unchanged on October 29, the euro is beholden to French developments and the dollar, they say. Monex sees $1.11 as the "key downside marker" for the euro and thinks gains will prove limited while French fiscal uncertainty and the Gulf conflict persist. The euro rises 0.2% to $1.1242 after earlier reaching a 10-day high of $1.1269, according to LSEG.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0907 ET - Treasury yields edge higher but are on pace to end the week with a decline as markets increasingly price in an interest rate hold by the Fed this month. Chairman Warsh stops short of giving forward guidance, as officials head to the blackout period preceding the FOMC meeting. Inflation remains a concern in financial markets, but the risk of economic slowdown due to steep borrowing costs keeps a lid on yields. U.S. import prices rise more than expected in September. The 10-year yield is at 5.115%, compared to 5.086% yesterday and 5.243% a week ago. The two-year is at 4.768%, up from 4.747% yesterday and down from 4.789% last week. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.co; @ptrevisani)

0808 ET - The dollar's falls could prove short-lived given the prospect of further tightening by the Federal Reserve, Trade Nation's David Morrison says in a note. The dollar is weaker as investors seem convinced the Fed will leave rates unchanged on October 28 after some policymakers recently signalled no rush to raise rates further, he says.However, once November's midterms are over, the Fed could be forced to raise rates "rather aggressively" if inflation continues to rise. The DXY dollar index trades within a band of support between 101.20 and 101.50, and if it can hold above here, it could resume rising, he says. The DXY falls 0.4% to 101.674 after earlier reaching a two-week low of 101.576.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0649 ET - The euro has received a boost from this week's unease over U.S. artificial intelligence stocks and could be entering a decent consolidative phase after recent losses, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The euro could rise to $1.1340-$1.1350, he says. "But do not expect euro-dollar to be the big outperformer on a further U.S. equity correction." A lower dollar versus the Swiss franc would likely take the lead in this case, he says. The euro rises 0.4% to a one-week high of $1.1263, having reached a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. The dollar falls to a two-week low of 0.8228 francs. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Hedge fund Two Sigma ends real estate unit fundraising, cuts staff - report
data.description:
Quantitative hedge fund Two Sigma Investments has halted efforts to raise $2B for its real estate investment unit and cut senior staff, as rising interest rates hobbled its fundraising efforts, according to a media report on Friday.

The unit's partner and chief investment officer, Rich Gomel, is leaving the company. Others on the real estate leadership team, including two of the three remaining partners and one of the two heads of data science, are also departing, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The firm, which had targeted raising ~$2B for the business, pulled in less than half that amount, some of the people told Bloomberg. Some of the real estate team will remain to manage its existing portfolio of properties.

Rising interest rates have weighed on commercial property valuations and led to owners holding assets for longer. Bloomberg, citing data from PEI Group, noted that private real estate fundraising totaled just over $30B for Q3 2026, the lowest quarterly total since early 2013.

Two Sigma started forming the real estate business in 2019 and launched it with internal capital about two years later. It was led by former Blackstone Vice Chair Tom Hill, who left the firm last year, one of the people told Bloomberg.

The business started taking outside capital in 2024 with its Real Estate Opportunity Fund, which mostly focused on housing and industrial investments, with some selective stakes in hospitality and office real estate. The hedge fund's strategy was to use the firm's data to power predictive tools that could project supply and demand, which would determine investment decisions.

data.title: Nvidia and Mercedes-Benz Extend AI Driving Deal
data.description:
Mercedes-Benz (MBGAF) and Nvidia are expanding their work on automated vehicles, with the latest phase bringing together onboard computing, AI-driven driving decisions and additional safety protections as they pursue more advanced driving capabilities.

A key objective is to prepare for SAE Level 4 applications, in which vehicles can operate autonomously within defined conditions. The companies identified robolimousines as a potential application, but did not provide a timetable for deployment.

The development will draw on several technologies. Mercedes-Benz's MB.OS supports vehicle functions and remote software updates, while Nvidia's Hyperion provides the computing and sensor framework. Nvidia's Alpamayo Stack is designed to help vehicles interpret driving situations and make decisions using AI reasoning.

The partnership also incorporates Nvidia Halos, which adds a separate safety layer intended to provide backup protections. Planned capabilities include navigating urban routes between destinations, automated parking and active safety functions.

For Mercedes-Benz, the extended collaboration could help bring more driving features into its software platform. Nvidia gains a continued role in the automaker's automated-driving development. Neither company provided additional commercial terms or a launch schedule in the supplied announcement.

data.title: Euro zone bonds steady after safe-haven rally, French debt set for best week since August
data.description:
Key points:
  • Money markets fully price chance of ECB rate rise in December
  • French 10-year yield premium over Bunds narrows to about 138 bps
  • IMF expects one more ECB rate hike this year

By Amanda Cooper

Euro zone government bond yields steadied on Friday but were still set for a weekly decline, thanks to bonds' recent safe-haven rally sparked by concern about AI-related companies' ability to deliver a return on their vast spending.

Global bonds are heading for their strongest weekly performance in four months, with yields on the sovereign debt of G7 economies down by an average of 8.7 basis points to 4.273%, according to LSEG data.

The shares and bonds of more indebted companies linked to the artificial intelligence build out were hit hard earlier this week, which weighed on the broader equity market and pushed investors back into bonds.

Yields on German 10-year Bunds (DE10YT=RR), the safe haven of choice for many investors in European assets, have fallen nearly 7 bps this week to around 3.42% on Friday, though were up 1 bp on the day. Two-year yields (DE2YT=RR) were 2 bps lower on Friday at 3.06%.

"Concerns about the AI boom are making government bonds look like better value," said analysts at Societe Generale.

However, "we have been here before" they cautioned, saying they doubted this was the end of the AI investment frenzy and the end of the cycle.

Government debt, which traditionally acts as a shock absorber for ructions in riskier assets, has been unable to perform this function for most of this year, as the surge in energy and food prices as a result of the Middle East war has forced investors to price in the prospect of higher borrowing costs in the form of higher yields.

The correlation between Bunds and the STOXX 600 , for example, has turned positive — meaning yields are more likely to fall when stocks fall and vice versa — this week for the first time since early August.

This relationship reached its most negative on record in late September, according to LSEG data.

As well as the impact of the war in the Gulf, central bankers from the world's largest economies gathering in Bangkok said the AI boom was also creating fresh inflation pressures and financial risks, because the investment is arriving long before the productivity gains AI promises.

FRENCH DEBT STABILISES

One of the major aggravating factors for bonds has been the persistent concern among investors about the long-term finances of developed-market governments.

Yields on French bonds (FR10YT=RR), which have been among the most harshly punished in the past few weeks, given the deep-rooted worry about France's ability to tackle its finances, were trading around 4.79%, flat on the day, and down 7 bps this week, set for their largest weekly drop since early August.

The premium of French 10-year yields over Bunds (DE10FR10=RR), a reflection of the extra compensation investors want for the risk of lending to France, rather than Germany, was around 137 bps on Friday, having fallen from a 15-year high of nearly 160 bps on October 2.

"We remain defensive on (French) OATs given the fiscal and political risks," said Soc Gen.

"Beware of new waves of volatility as the budget debate is ongoing and investors are not keen to add a lot of risk."

Money markets show traders do not believe the ECB will raise interest rates at its meeting this month, but upped the chances of a December rate hike to 100%, from just below that level earlier in the day. At least one more hike is priced in by next April (0#EURIRPR).

There was little reaction to data that showed harmonised inflation in the euro zone ran at a five-year high of 3.8% in September, in line with expectations in a Reuters poll of economists.

The IMF said in its regular forecast for Europe it expects one more ECB rate hike this year.

data.title: Italy clinches deal with EU over measures to limit impact of gas prices on electricity costs
data.description:
Italy said on Friday it had clinched a deal with European Union authorities over measures to limit the impact of sky-high gas prices on electricity costs for households and businesses.

  • The measures are in line with the rules on state aid, the office of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said in a statement.

  • Rome will act to preserve equal conditions in the internal market, Meloni's office said.

  • As a result of the deal, "Italy will notify the Commission of the temporary measures in accordance with EU state aid rules, and the Commission will assess them as a matter of priority."

  • The statement did not explain the terms of the agreement.

data.title: JB Hunt Gets Analysts Talking Post Q3 Report: JPMorgan Says Most Investors ‘Overestimate’ How Quickly Margins Can Improve
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan lowered its price target to $283 from $287, maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating, while cautioning that investors may overestimate how quickly Intermodal margins can improve.
  • Morgan Stanley lowered its price target to $195 from $200 and maintained an ‘Underweight’ rating.
  • JB Hunt’s revenue reached $3.68 billion, exceeding Fiscal AI’s $3.58 billion estimate, while net earnings edged up to $172.4 million from $170.8 million a year earlier.

JB Hunt (JBHT) shares drew investor attention on Friday after several analysts lowered their price targets following the company’s third-quarter earnings, as higher operating costs and margin pressure tempered its strong revenue growth.

According to The Fly, Wells Fargo lowered its price target to $285 from $305 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm said the third-quarter cost trend was as expected, while the intermodal pricing outlook was better despite slower volume.

Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on the stock to $195 from $200 and maintained an ‘Underweight’ rating. According to The Fly, analyst Ravi Shanker said the third quarter laid bare cost pressures flagged at the Laguna conference a month earlier, adding that a recovery through pricing would take time and effort.

Meanwhile, JPMorgan lowered its target to $283 from $287 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm said the wide discount to truckload is still pulling through record conversion activity, but “most investors continue to overestimate how quickly JBI margins can improve.”

The company reported diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.82, up from $1.76 a year earlier, compared with analysts’ estimate of $1.80, according to Fiscal AI. However, operating income increased 2% to $247.1 million, while operating margin narrowed to 6.7% from 7.9% a year earlier.

data.title: U.S. Industrial Production Faces Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description: A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." data.title: US tells election officials to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of midterms
data.description:
The FBI and the US cyber defense agency CISA are urging election officials — and the American public — to be on guard against AI-powered tricks ahead of next month's midterm elections.

Here are more details:

  • An alert issued Friday by CISA and the FBI says that hackers may try to disrupt the midterm elections using bogus text messages and emails aimed at stealing passwords or other sensitive data.

  • The alert says that "election officials, candidates, and their political organizations are attractive targets to malicious cyber criminals."

  • The alert says that "super intelligence," a Trump-approved term for AI, is allowing hackers to sharpen their rogue emails and texts to make them look and sound more convincing.

data.title: Data double-dip: Industrial production, import prices
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dow gains, S&P 500 edges down, Nasdaq declines
  • Materials lead S&P 500 sectot gainers; just tech, communication services red
  • Euro STOXX 600 index up ~0.7%
  • Dollar falls; US crude, bitcoin slip; gold up slightly
  • US 10-year Treasury yield flat at ~5.09%

DATA DOUBLE-DIP: INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION, IMPORT PRICES

Investors were treated to two economic indicators on Friday, capping a week chock-full of them. And both arrived hotter than economists anticipated.

First, industrial output (USIP=ECI) grew by 0.7% last month, marking a solid acceleration from August's 0.1% growth and coming in stronger than the 0.4% analysts expected.

Manufacturing output growth rebounded from the previous month's 0.2% decline, rising 0.3%, in line with consensus.

Beneath the surface, the 3.0% drop in motor vehicles/parts was offset by a 3.5% surge in utilities and a 1.0% rise in construction supplies. A 1.5% increase in high-tech output suggests AI-related demand isn't going anywhere. Excluding high-tech, output rose 0.6%.

Year-on-year, industrial output has risen 2.2%.

Capacity utilization (USCAPU=ECI), a measure of economic slack, tightened by half a percentage point to 76.9%, the highest since December 2023.

"The AI-capex boom probably will continue to lift output in a few tech-adjacent industries, but other manufacturing sectors will remain sluggish," writes Oliver Allen, senior US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. "A continued gradual recovery in manufacturing, rather than a boom, is likely in the months ahead."

Separately, the cost of goods imported to the United States (USIMP=ECI) (excluding tariffs) jumped by 1.1% last month, per Labor Department data, hotter than the 0.9% economists predicted and more than double August's 0.5% increase.

Digging deeper, a 4.6% rise in imported petroleum prices and a 2.7% increase in industrial supplies put upward pressure on the headline. Year-on-year, prices of imported petroleum and industrial supplies have risen 35.4% and 20.4%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the cost of US exports rose 2.2% versus the 1.1% consensus, driven by a 4.0% pop in industrial supplies and a 2.7% increase in food/feed/drinks.

Year-over-year, import prices have jumped 8.1%, and export prices have surged 11.6%.

It's the third indicator released this week — following CPI and PPI — to show the extent to which energy price pressures arising from the Iran war are morphing into a broader, more systemic inflation.

As a result, markets are recalibrating their expectations regarding central bank monetary policy.

"We're looking for inflation to accelerate in the near term but not plateau at a higher level,” writes Oren Klachkin, financial market economist at Nationwide. “The heated near-term increases will give way to tamer readings down the road in 2027."

"That said, the risk is inflation remains higher for longer than we expect and is more difficult for the Fed to vanquish."

data.title: Broker tips: Broker tips: Bridgepoint, Pulsar Helium
data.description:
Berenberg, which reiterated its 'buy' rating on the stock, said stronger‑than‑expected performance‑related earnings across FY26-28, driven initially by Energy Capital Partners Fund V and later by both ECP and private equity, had prompted the valuation change.

Bridgepoint has now upgraded guidance three times this year, with Berenberg stating the exceptional returns in ECP V were behind the FY26 PRE uplift, with one asset, ProEnergy, expected to deliver substantial carry on its own. PRE guidance for FY27-28 has also been raised, reflecting broader contributions from ECP funds and strong value creation in private equity.

Fundraising targets have been exceeded, highlighted Berenberg, with the increased €28bn goal for FY24-26 already being met and the total now expected to reach around €30bn.

Berenberg said the combination of higher management‑fee visibility and upgraded PRE across FY26-28 meant profits and cash generation should rise significantly.

Bridgepoint has rebased its FY26 dividend per share from 10p to 15p, equivalent to around 40% to 45% of EPS, and plans to distribute 40% to 60% of cash profits thereafter through ordinary dividends and top‑ups via specials or buybacks.

Berenberg noted that its fundraising assumptions were already close to the new guidance, so changes there were limited. However, the PRE upgrades drove a 40% increase to its FY26 EPS forecast and an 8% uplift for FY27, while dividend per share estimates rose 56% to 96% across FY26-28, in line with the updated distribution policy.

The German bank also raised the multiples used in its valuation framework, citing stronger fundraising, better‑than‑expected fund returns, higher embedded value, best‑in‑class underlying earnings margins and an enhanced capital‑distribution profile. FRE and PRE multiples moved from 12x/6x to 15x/7.5x, respectively.

Over at Canaccord Genuity, analysts initiated coverage of Pulsar Helium with a 'speculative buy' rating and a 150p target price on Friday, noting the group was advancing a major primary helium resource at its Topaz project in Minnesota.

The Canadian broker believes Topaz contains more than 1bn cubic feet of recoverable helium, well above the 380m cu ft P50 estimate in the 2024 CPR, after Pulsar successfully encountered helium in seven wells drilled to date.

Pulsar has lined up Chart Industries to supply equipment for a helium plant with around 5m cu meteres per year capacity and contracted up to six additional production wells, with total development costs estimated at $175m.

Canaccord said the tight global helium market - with around 25% of supply offline - supports strong pricing for years to come, and forecasts Pulsar generating over $130m in net profit from FY29 onwards.

First production was expected as early as Q1 2029, supported by recent legislative changes in Minnesota, with key catalysts ahead including a resource update, sales contracts and funding progress at Topaz.

Reporting by Iain Gilbert at Sharecast.com

data.title: South Africa to open payments system to retailers, telecoms, fintechs in 2027
data.description:
Key points:
  • Non-banks expected to go live around March 2027 after licensing
  • Direct access ends banks' intermediary role in national clearing and settlement
  • Central bank says overhaul aims to cut costs and widen digital finance access
  • Central bank to launch white-label ATM pilot in January

By Nqobile Dludla and Kopano Gumbi

South Africa will open its payments system to non-bank operators, including telecoms firms, fintechs and retailers, from mid-2027, a central bank official said on Friday, as part of a major overhaul of the system.

The change would end banks' longstanding dominance of South Africa's payments processing market, allowing non-bank firms to connect directly to the national payments infrastructure, which clears and settles payments nationwide, rather than relying on banks as intermediaries.

The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) hopes the reform will spur competition, lower costs, broaden access to digital financial services and encourage innovation in a sector increasingly challenged by fintech companies and mobile-money providers such as MTN .

Pradeep Maharaj, executive director of SARB's Payments Ecosystem Modernisation (PEM) programme, told a media roundtable that rules governing payment activities and exemptions would be published by November. Non-bank participants are expected to go live around March 2027 following licensing, allowing time for testing and systems integration ahead of a mid-year launch.

The reform is a key pillar of the central bank's PEM programme, which aims to reduce reliance on cash and accelerate the adoption of affordable digital payments.

SARB plans to modernise payment infrastructure, increase adoption of fast-payment services like PayShap and strengthen security and digital identity verification.

Maharaj said the changes should lower transaction costs for small businesses and consumers and reduce cash dependency, while giving unbanked and underserved consumers wider access to digital payments.

As part of the wider modernisation effort, SARB has also proposed creating a national cash utility, a central bank-owned cash handling company, and introducing "white-label" ATMs operated as shared infrastructure rather than by individual banks, in a bid to lower cash-handling costs and preserve access to cash, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

Maharaj said SARB expects to migrate its cash centres into the new cash utility in 2027 and begin incorporating industry-owned centres, which will be bought by the utility, by the end of next year.

He added that a white-label ATM pilot would be launched in January, with the first batch of machines set to be rolled out nationwide by the end of next year.

data.title: US federal bankruptcy court operations disrupted by cybersecurity incident
data.description:
By AJ Vicens

Several online services supporting US federal courts' bankruptcy systems have gone offline following a cybersecurity incident involving a court contractor, the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOC) said on Thursday.

BAE Systems IT, a division of the British defense contractor BAE Systems , operates the Bankruptcy Noticing Center's (BNC) systems and websites on behalf of the federal judiciary, the AOC said in a statement.

  • BAE is "actively investigating this incident and working to restore operations," the AOC said in the statement.

  • A BAE Systems spokesperson said on Friday that the company is "aware of a security incident that is isolated to the BNC system" and has taken immediate steps to address it. BAE Systems is "coordinating closely" with the courts on the response, the spokesperson said.

  • All access to the BNC systems and websites BAE operates on behalf of the judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process is unavailable, the AOC said.

  • The BNC "produces and transmits bankruptcy notices for all federal bankruptcy courts around the country," the AOC said.

  • Affected websites include bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov as well as the National Creditor Registration Service.

  • The incident also "halted the BNC's production and distribution of bankruptcy notices for bankruptcy courts," the AOC said.

data.title: Eli Lilly Wins EU Backing for Foundayo Weight-Loss Pill
data.description:
Eli Lilly and Co. (LLY, Financials), the pharmaceutical company, moved a step closer to launching its oral weight-loss drug in Europe.

A key European Medicines Agency panel issued a positive opinion on Foundayo, also known as orforglipron, for weight management and treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults.

The recommendation now goes to the European Commission, which will make the final decision on marketing authorization.

The opportunity is obvious, but so is the competitive pressure.

Novo Nordisk already won EU approval in July for its once-daily Wegovy pill, giving it an early lead in a market where patients may prefer tablets over injections.

That makes speed important for Lilly.

If Foundayo wins final approval, Lilly would gain another way to expand its obesity franchise while competing more directly with Novo for patients looking for oral GLP-1 treatments.

For investors, the bigger question is whether pills can broaden the weight-loss market enough to support growth beyond injectable therapies.

The next thing to watch is the European Commission's final ruling and how quickly Lilly can launch Foundayo if approval comes through.

data.title: Tesla shares rise 4% after Elon Musk unveils redesigned Roadster with SpaceX thrusters
data.description:
Tesla shares rose 4% in pre-market trade on Friday to $375 apiece after the electric vehicle maker unveiled its redesigned Roadster featuring compressed-air thrusters developed with SpaceX. SpaceX shares also climbed 1%.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk showcased the long-anticipated sports car at a SpaceX test facility in McGregor, Texas, on Thursday (local time). A livestreamed demonstration showed the driverless vehicle launching off a ramp, performing a mid-air flip and landing on its wheels. The vehicle was also shown accelerating from zero to 60 miles per hour in under a second.

“Turns out the future does have flying cars,” Musk said at the event, according to ANI.

Tesla
@Tesla

Real life, baby https://t.co/3QEqn18wig

Oct 16, 2026

The Roadster uses advanced cold-gas thrusters operated by electric actuators to deliver precise thrust and help stabilise the vehicle during flight. The system is designed to support rapid acceleration and manoeuvres, while a multi-mode suction system generates downforce by drawing air from beneath the car.

According to Tesla, the suction system can generate enough force to hold the vehicle upside down, even when stationary. Powered fans and active aerodynamic wings are designed to improve traction and cornering performance, including at low speeds.

The redesigned vehicle also features a next-generation steer-by-wire system that adjusts feedback to different road conditions. Its Track Mode lowers the car and modifies its suspension, while high-downforce and low-drag settings can be activated depending on track requirements.

Tesla Roadster variants and features

Tesla has outlined two versions of the redesigned vehicle. The Thrust variant, planned as a limited release, is designed for two occupants and combines a multi-mode suction system with rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters. The company says the configuration enables acceleration from zero to 60 mph in under a second.

The rocket variant, meanwhile, is designed to accommodate one occupant and is described as air-ready, although it has not yet been approved for road use. Its cold-gas thrusters are positioned around the vehicle's perimeter to enable forward and upward acceleration, as well as lateral and rotational movement.

Tesla highlighted the role of the thruster system in overcoming the limitations of conventional tyre grip.

“Every car on the road today is limited by one thing: tire grip Roadster's thruster system generates 4–5x the force the tires can. More force on the same mass means significantly better acceleration – physics does the rest,” Tesla said on X.

The company also described the vehicle as a pilot-focused car, citing its active aerodynamics, multi-mode suction system and cold-gas thrusters.

Roadster has faced multiple delays

The latest unveiling follows years of delays since Tesla first announced the next-generation Roadster in 2017. The original Roadster, the company's first product, was launched in 2008 and discontinued in 2012.

While the latest demonstration showcased the vehicle's ability to perform aerial manoeuvres, the technology's commercial deployment and the prospect of flying cars becoming a regular feature on roads remain uncertain.

The unveiling brings together Tesla's electric vehicle engineering and SpaceX's propulsion technology, although the company has yet to establish when the redesigned Roadster will be available to customers.

(With ANI inputs)
